notes: Contraction mirror of biology-replace-0015. The revision edit is derived (penicillin was discovered in the United Kingdom, from the discoverer and his workplace), so the contraction removes its main stored premise: penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming. Relation: has_discoverer, a new functional relation (a discovery is credited to one discoverer or team) with the inverse discoverer_of, both staged, because discovered_by in RELATIONS.md is neither functional nor many-valued and an existing relation's tags cannot be changed from staging. Cardinality question: Marie Curie as another candidate discoverer ('no' before, 'does not know' after); Howard Florey and Ernst Chain were avoided because they shared the 1945 Nobel Prize and text credits them with developing penicillin, so 'no' is not clear-cut. Related near is the inverse; related far binds the subject through the description the revision already checks. The derived questions take the discoverer by description and look up two facts stored about Fleming by name (birth country, birth year). Questions about the country of the discovery, London or St Mary's Hospital were dropped: they are stored separately and survive the removal of the discoverer. related[1]: functional, the removed fact asked as yes/no (has_discoverer is functional); the paired revision (a derived edit on discovery_country) has only one related query, so this mirrors the removed fact rather than a revision query.
